text: Agent Rory. Sit down. Last night the Royal Observatory in Greenwich was robbed.
They took the plans for the Helios Lens: a forty-metre mirror in orbit, built to beam a little sunshine onto cloudy cities.
Only if you point it the other way, it can throw a whole city into darkness at noon.
The night guard says he saw nothing. He is lying. Prove it, find the thief, and follow the plans wherever they go.
Your Spy Watch will show the objective. I'll be in your ear the whole way. Dave's outside with the cab.
The lights of the world are in your hands, Agent Rory. Don't drop them.
Agent Rory. For the first time in eleven years I am going to smile. There. Did you see it?
The Eclipse Engine is in pieces, Sterling is in a cell, and Kolya has asked for seconds.
And Madame Eclipse is out there somewhere in the snow, plotting. Which means we'll need you again.
The world stays bright because of you. This medal is yours. Now go and sleep. That is an order.
Three weeks, Agent Rory. That is how long the world was safe.
Madame Eclipse has surfaced in Paris, and she is taking orders. UMBRA has a Chairman. Nobody has ever seen his face.
We intercepted one message: "Seven lanterns. One midnight." Seven little mirrors on balloons, hidden over seven cities.
At the next new moon they all light at once. Seven capitals go dark, and the ransom is the sunrise.
Each lantern has a different lock, a different city and a different UMBRA cell guarding it. Seven lanterns, and a supply line running through two more cities besides.
Find them. Put them out. And find the Chairman. Kolya, by the way, escaped in a bread van. Of course he did.
Agent Rory. Seven lanterns, seven countries, one Chairman, and a Madame Eclipse in the back of a black cab.
The Chairman's mountain is now a very expensive dairy. Real cows this time.
Chip shop gives me free chips. Is fair. Is finally fair.
Two medals, Agent Rory. Nobody in the history of M.I.S.T. has two. Try not to lose them.
Thank you, Commander. Same time next week?
Agent Rory. The Chairman has been talking. Not to us; to his lawyer. But his mountain kept better records than he did.
Every lantern, every mirror, every Eclipse Engine was built for a buyer. One name in the ledger: the Curator.
He collects things nobody can own. The last thing on his list is the Northern Lights.
Seven Prism Keys turn the Aurora Engine, under the ice at the bottom of the world. It pulls the lights out of the sky and into his vault, and every compass and every satellite goes with them.
He has four of them already. His people lifted them out of Istanbul, Marrakech, Reykjavik and Singapore, in each case about a week after you left.
Three are still loose. The fifth is somewhere above Machu Picchu, the sixth is in Amsterdam, and the seventh is already sitting in the engine.
I know his face. He never paid me for Siberia. I come too. I bring chips.
Peru first, Agent Rory. And pack a coat for the end of it.
Agent Rory. Seven Prism Keys, four of them lifted straight back out of his own vault, and one Curator in a very cold cell.
The Aurora Engine is now the world's biggest fridge. Dr Okafor's penguins have moved in.
He paid me. Finally. With a stolen painting. Is problem.
Three medals. I have had to order a bigger drawer. Go home. Sleep. That is, as always, an order.
Thank you, Commander. What's on his list after the Northern Lights?
The moon, probably. Sleep first.
A five-star UMBRA lock. Guess a code and it tells you how many symbols are right and in the right place, and how many are right but in the wrong place.
Use every answer. Eight guesses is plenty for a spy.
It's open. And the door log says it was opened at fourteen minutes past two. From the INSIDE.
Then somebody let them in. The night guard is called Nigel Pratt. Ask him. Nicely, then not nicely.
I never saw nothing. Nothing at all. I was at my desk with my tea.
He's wired to the polygraph. Smooth waves mean the truth. Jumpy spikes mean a fib. Some fibs are sneaky and small, so watch closely.
Alright! ALRIGHT! A lady with a voice like silk paid me. I let a man in. Fingers Malone.
He's hiding in the flat above the chip shop on Baker Street. Please don't tell my mum.
Good work. Dave has been parked outside that flat for an hour. Ask him what his camera saw.
My dashcam takes a picture of that flat every ten minutes, guv. Here's one from before Fingers legged it and one from after.
Spot everything that changed between the two pictures. Tap the differences on the right-hand one.
The painting of the horse has moved. There's something behind it. A safe!
And he's took the telly. Charming.
A safe behind the painting. Four numbers on this one, Vi.
My stethoscope gadget. Drag the dial round; the closer you get to a number, the louder the tick. When the light goes green, tap SET. Four numbers and the door opens.
A letter. "The blueprints go to Venice. The Glassmaker will build the lens. Carnival night, Murano." Signed E.
And a photograph. A woman in dark glasses.
Oh no. That's Madame Eclipse. Head of UMBRA. If she's got the Helios plans, the whole world's in trouble.
Big fella in two coats just got into a launch at the steps. Down the river he goes. I'd take you myself but I don't do water.
M.I.S.T. has a boat at the steps, Rory. Drag left and right to steer. Clip a buoy and he gains on you; keep it clean and you will reel him in.
He jumped onto a barge and legged it, but he left his bag. Chips, a spare coat, and a boarding pass. Venice, tonight.
Knew it. Nobody eats chips that fast unless they've a plane to catch.
His order book. Every page is gibberish. It's in code.
A cipher wheel. Every letter has been slid along the alphabet. Drag the inner ring until the words come out. He signs everything VETRI.
"One mirror lens, forty metres, for Madame E." Forty metres! That's bigger than a house.
Page two: "Payment arrives at the carnival. The courier wears the golden mask."
And the delivery note will be in his ring vault. Nobody has opened that vault since his grandmother.
Three glass rings, each with a notch. Drag a ring to turn it and line every notch up at the top.
Careful: some rings drag their neighbour round with them. Start from the middle and work outwards.
The delivery note. "Lens crated Thursday. Courier pays in gold at the carnival, then takes the manifest to the loft."
Then to the piazza! Half of Venice is wearing gold tonight.
Twenty masked dancers and one of them is UMBRA's courier. I'll feed you clues on the watch.
Tap the one who matches every clue. Tap a tourist and you'll just get told off in Italian.
Got you! And the manifest? "In the loft, behind the lasers," he says. Lasers?
UMBRA rented the loft over the bakery. It hums at night. I thought it was the ovens.
Sweeping laser beams. Touch one and the alarm sends you back to the door. Drag to move, and wait for a gap.
The manifest is on the desk at the far end.
"One lens, crated. Transfer at Istanbul. Onward port to follow." That's all it says.
Then we know where it changes ships and not where it ends up. Istanbul, Agent Rory. Emre sells tea by the ferry and misses nothing.
There's a print on that glass. Lift it, then match it against the prints on file. Look at the middle of the print first: rings, a loop or an arch.
It matches a shipping agent called Mr Silver. He signs for UMBRA's cargo all round the Mediterranean.
And he signals ships from the Maiden's Tower, it says here. Go and watch it.
The lighthouse is blinking in Morse. A short flash is a dot, a long flash is a dash. The chart is on your watch; spell out what it says.
It spells DOCK. But there's no crate on any dock, and the water under the bazaar has gone down half a metre.
The cistern. I told you those pumps were suspicious.
The pump room's wiring is a bird's nest. Follow each wire from its number to its letter with your eyes, then tap the terminal it reaches. Don't guess.
Pumps off, water back, and the crate's down there at the bottom. It's empty. The lens went on without it.
Then find the paperwork, Rory. Somebody had to stamp that crate.
The customs seal is under one of those cups, and the trader is about to shuffle them. Keep your eyes on the right one and do not blink.
Got it. Stamped for Alexandria, and written underneath in pencil: Cairo, the Great Pyramid, Thursday noon.
So Venice was right and we have not lost a day. Egypt, Agent Rory. Dr Farouk is expecting you.
Their relay's still switched on. Drag the needle along the band. Less crackle means you're getting warm.
There are two UMBRA channels tonight, and a pop station in between. Find them both and hold each one.
That was HER. "Fetch the Eye from the tomb." Whatever the Eye is, the Engine can't focus without it.
The Eye of Ra. A crystal lens the old astronomers kept in the tomb of light. Sealed for three thousand years. The door is opened by stone and by sunlight, in that order.
Three stone discs on the first pillar. Move them all to the third pillar, one at a time, and never put a big disc on a small one.
It's the oldest puzzle in the world. The old builders were showing off.
The discs are across and something's grinding inside the ridge.
The light chamber. Now the sun does the rest.
A beam of sun comes through the door. Tap the bronze mirrors to turn them and steer it onto the sun disc.
Stone blocks stop the beam, and some mirrors are only there to confuse you. Two chambers.
The door's opening... and there it is. The Eye of Ra. It's warm.
Hey! Little spy! That is MY crystal! ...Is not fair.
First time we've beaten them to it! Now they'll need a computer chip to focus that mirror instead. But where have they gone?
I've got a satellite picture of the airfield, but it came down in scrambled tiles. Put them back in the right order.
Tap a tile, then tap the square it belongs in, and the two swap over. The little picture on the right is what it should look like.
A plane on the runway, tail number UMB-7. The flight plan has one stop before Asia: Marrakech.
And they unloaded something there. Find out what, Rory, before it reaches a laboratory.
One of those coins is a fake, and it's heavier. You get a few weighings: tap coins to put them on either pan, weigh, and think. Then accuse the fake.
That one. Of course. He also bought a map, torn into pieces, from the stall across the lane.
The map's name is in pieces. Unscramble the letters: tap them in the right order to spell the word. The clue is on the card.
The word on the map is a camp out past the palm groves. The camel men's camp.
The camel men's chart shows a constellation. Find the same shape in the sky and join its stars in order. Plenty of stars up there aren't part of it.
The stars point straight back into the city: a riad with a blue door and a very high roof.
Nobody's letting you in at the door. Grapple gun: drag to set the angle and the power, and hook the ledge on the roof.
Hooked, climbed, and there's a flight case in a birdcage up here. The bird's fine.
Inside: the lens's mirror mount, with an empty socket where its guidance chip should be. And a shipping label. Kaito Labs, Tokyo.
A mount with no brain in it. They are going to Japan to buy one. Tokyo, Agent Rory.
I watched the guard type the code from across the street. I remember the pattern. Watch the keys light up, then press them in the same order.
Three codes, each one longer, and they get quicker.
We're in. But there's a corridor of red lines between us and the lift.
Lasers. Kaito likes lasers.
Four beams this time, and they sweep faster. Drag to move. Wait for the gap, then go.
Floor forty-four... the chip cabinet's empty. Someone took it an hour ago.
They left through the server room. Servers remember everything. Come.
The data lines are scrambled. Tap the tiles to turn them. Connect the port on the left to the port on the right.
Bigger boards than a hobby kit. Two of them.
The log is here but it's locked behind the root password.
Then we crack the password.
Four symbols again, but six to choose from. The terminal tells you how many are right and in place, and how many are right but misplaced.
"Chip shipped. Paid by STERLING HOLDINGS, New York. Forty million dollars."
"Contact: Marcus Sterling. Sterling Tower, penthouse."
Sterling. Wall Street's slipperiest banker. New York, Agent Rory. Detective Romano will meet you.
Two photos of the penthouse, kid. Monday and this morning. Something moved. Find everything that's different.
The bookcase has swung out. There's a vault door behind it. And the desk lamp's gone.
Pin-tumbler vault. Six pins. Your Aunt Vi's gonna love this.
Six pins. The marker bounces up and down each one. Tap PICK when it's in the green. Miss and a pin drops. They get quicker.
It's open. A ledger. "Paid: one mirror, Venice. One chip, Tokyo. One rocket, Brazil."
"Ship rocket from Rio de Janeiro, Pier 9." A ROCKET? And... Sal, something in here is ticking.
Oh, that's not good. That's really not good.
UMBRA rigged it to burn the ledger. Seventy seconds. Four devices this time.
The manual's on your watch. Read the rules in order and cut the first wire that fits.
It stopped. The ledger's last page is a bit singed. "Rocket sails Friday. Pier 9, Rio. Crate marked ZIMA."
Nice work, kid. And there's something else in this office. It's been squeaking at my radio all week.
An UMBRA transmitter is hidden somewhere in that office. My sniffer pings a square and tells you how many steps away the bug is.
Ten pings. Use the numbers to narrow it down before you tap FOUND.
Got it. Inside the globe. It's tuned to a harbour channel in Rio: Pier 9's crane.
Then Zima is not a person, it is a place, and it is where that rocket is going. Rio, Agent Rory. Friday is the day after tomorrow.
The crew photos are face down on the desk. Flip two at a time and find the matching pairs. Every pair is a crew member.
Remember where you saw each face.
A pair I know. "K. Zima, cook." Kolya's on the crew of the Severnaya.
Then the Severnaya is our ship. Let's get a look at her.
My camera. Drag to aim, slide the zoom, hold the target in the ring until it focuses, then SNAP. Four photographs this time.
The crate says ZIMA STATION. The ship is the Severnaya. Kolya's on the quay with a coconut, and the crane's cab has an UMBRA logo.
Zima means winter. Somewhere very, very cold. We need to know exactly where. Tonight, the yard.
Four guards with torches, and a searchlight on the crane. Stay out of the light and slip between the containers.
Drag to move. Reach the crate and the tracker plants itself. Spotted, and it's back to the fence.
Tracker's pinging! Sixty-four degrees north, one hundred degrees east. Siberia. Zima Station.
And the launch is in three days. Get me a picture of that place before you fly.
The satellite's over Siberia now. Sixteen tiles this time. Swap them home and we'll see what Zima Station looks like.
A fortress in the snow, a rocket on a pad, a boiler-room door on the west side and a lit window on the east.
Pack a coat, Agent Rory. Two coats.
The shredder bin. Ten strips. Kolya is thorough, but not clever.
Drag the strips back into order, then tape it. The abort code should be on there somewhere.
"ECLIPSE ENGINE. Launch at midnight. ABORT CODE..." four symbols. I've got them, Vi.
The reactor is next door. If we stall it, the countdown pauses. Briefly.
Four fuel rods. Move the stack to the cooling rack on the right, one rod at a time, never a big one on a small one.
Same puzzle as the tomb, with one more rod. That's twice the moves.
The rods are in the rack. The clock's paused at T-minus ninety.
For ninety seconds, once the vault door opens. Hurry.
Four steel rings, and every one drags its outer neighbour. Innermost first, then work outwards.
It's open. That's the control room. And that's HER on the big screen.
Agent Rory. You have come a very long way to watch the lights go out.
Eighty seconds, little spy. Then every city on Earth learns what midnight at noon feels like.
Ignore her. Three things, fast. Type the abort code. Turn the dial to the number on the screen. Then cut the wires by the rules.
Engines... off. Three seconds to spare. The Engine's just sitting on the pad.
Is not fair. I was eating a pirozhok.
We will meet again, little spy. Somewhere the sun still shines.
She took the snowmobile. Kolya took the pirozhok. You, Agent Rory, take the plane home.
Flowers! I deliver flowers. Tulips, roses, nothing else, I swear it.
He's on the polygraph. His fibs are sneakier than Nigel's, so watch for smaller spikes.
D'accord, d'accord! The crate is in the roof of the glass pyramid. A balloon, a mirror, a very nasty lock. And the lady in dark glasses paid me in cash.
The Louvre closes at six. After that, it belongs to the lasers.
Five beams in that gallery, and two of them go round and round. Take your time in the gaps.
I'm under the pyramid. The lantern's up in the roof, and its panel wants a five-symbol code.
Five symbols, six to pick from, nine guesses. Same rules as the Observatory door: use every answer it gives you.
The lantern's dark! And its memory chip names the next one: Nairobi, Kenya.
Before you go: Madame Eclipse is meeting someone at the Eiffel Tower tonight. Take the camera.
Four targets across the river: the lady herself, the person she's meeting, the van, and the crate. Zoom right in and hold steady.
The van says ALPINE DAIRY. The man has a grey moustache and never turns round.
A dairy van at the Eiffel Tower. The Chairman keeps cows, apparently. Nairobi, Agent Rory.
Au revoir, little spy. I do not take the stairs.
She has a rocket backpack. So do you now, Rory: strap in. Drag left and right to steer, and drag up and down to climb and dive.
Fly through the rings to stay on her line. Balloons, drones, birds, banners: hit one and she gains on you.
She ran out of fuel over the tower and came down in the river. Soaked, furious, and arrested.
This changes nothing. The Chairman has six more lanterns and no patience.
Six. And you have a rocket backpack. Nairobi, Agent Rory.
Two pictures from the same camera, one hour apart. Find everything that changed.
Truck tracks, a dropped crate lid, and an elephant that's moved... towards the old watering hole.
Elephants follow the tether cable. It hums.
The lantern's tether is buried somewhere on this grid. Nine pings. Each one tells you how many steps away it is.
Found the cable. It runs to a camp under the acacias, and the camp has guards.
Five guards, one searchlight, and a very sleepy lion on the far side. Do not wake the lion.
Reach the crate and read what's on it.
The crate says: DISARM FREQUENCY ON RANGER TOWER CHANNEL. Sneaky.
My old tower. The radio still works, if you kick it.
Two channels to find, and the lock window is narrow. Hold the needle dead still.
Lantern two's dark. And there's a second signal on that channel, from a very long way north.
Iceland. That is where the lantern mirrors are ground. Cut the supply and the rest of them are string and glue. Sigrún is expecting you.
Cross the lagoon one tile at a time. Every safe tile tells you how many of its neighbours are thin. Go through one and it's a cold bath and back to the start.
Across. Dry. And there's a drilling rig on the far shore with UMBRA's mark painted over.
Every drill shakes the ground its own way. Slide the dials until your wave lies exactly on top of the one Sigrún recorded, then lock it.
That is a diamond drill, two hundred metres down, in the old lava tube. Go in from the mountain side.
The tube is full of steam; you'll only see a few steps ahead. Tap the arrows to move. Where you've been stays lit. Find the way out the far end.
Out the far end, and it's the harbour. The drill was a decoy. They're not digging the glass, they're grinding it, and it goes out by boat.
The crane won't lift the boat's cargo until it balances. Tap a crate, then tap a slot on the deck. Weight times distance from the middle must match on both sides.
Balanced. The middle crate is full of mirror blanks packed in ice, and the label says AGRA.
Then your next lantern is in India. Mind the heat. You have been spoiled up here.
Twenty dancers and four clues this time. Tap the one who matches all of them.
Got him. A folded message in his pocket, and it's in code again.
Everyone in this town writes in code. It is a very old town.
Three pages, each with its own shift. She signs them E.
The lantern's in the sundial observatory, the lock opens with a beam of light, and then there's a keypad.
The observatory is stone and mirrors. The old astronomers would have liked you.
Three chambers this time, bigger each time, and plenty of mirrors that are only there to fool you.
The star disc is lit and the lantern's keypad has popped out of the stone.
I filmed Kolya typing three codes into it last week. He types with one finger. Watch, then copy.
Long ones. Say the numbers out loud.
Lantern three's dark. The memory chip says: Beijing, the Great Wall.
Mei runs a tea house by the wall. She also runs half of Beijing. Go.
The courier is running for the airport with the lantern's memory. My tuk-tuk is faster than his van. Probably. Hold on.
Steer round the carts, Rory. Clip one and he gains on you.
We ran him off at the gate. The memory chip is ours, and it doesn't name a city: it names a relay. Marina Bay, Singapore.
I told you. Faster than a van. Do not tell my mother about the fruit stall.
Each tower knows how far the drone is, not which way. Three circles, one crossing. Drag the marker to where all three rings meet and lock it.
Got the drone. It came down on the roof of the hawker centre, and it's carrying a spare control board.
The new menu board is a grid with numbers along the edges. The numbers say which squares to fill. Fill them all and a picture appears. Tap a wrong one and it marks itself; that's a slip.
It's a lightning bolt. Underneath it: GARDENS, MIDNIGHT.
Somebody has been leaning on the supertree's rail. Lift the print and match it. More prints on file this time, and they're closer to each other.
Mr Silver again. The same hand that signed for the lens in Istanbul, a whole operation ago.
Then he did not retire. Noted. Read the trees, Agent Rory.
The supertrees are blinking a longer word, faster. Watch it as many times as you need.
It spells BEIJING. This whole grove is the relay: it hands the lanterns their orders, and the next order is for the Great Wall.
Go. I will keep the noodles warm for about a week.
Four numbers, and the tick only starts when you're close. Slowly.
A map of the wall with a tower circled... but the circle's smudged. Three towers it could be.
Then look from above. My dish on the roof talks to the satellite. Sometimes.
Sixteen tiles, and a fiddly picture. Swap them home. Check each one against the little picture on the right.
The third tower has a balloon crate on its roof. That's the one.
Two big boards. Connect left to right and the lantern's lift comes down.
The lift's down. The lantern's on five stone rods, like the tomb in Cairo.
The old builders again. They travelled.
Five discs. Thirty-one moves if you don't waste any. Small disc first, and it always goes the same way round.
Lantern four's dark. Next: Sydney.
Matilda will meet you at the beach. Do not let her teach you to surf. There isn't time.
More faces this time. Flip two at a time and remember where they were.
The diver: a pair of photos, wetsuit, UMBRA badge on the tank. He surfaces at the bridge's south pylon.
Five targets round the harbour, and a swaying lens. Patience.
The diver, the hatch under the pylon, the balloon crate on the barge, the Opera House roof camera, and Kolya. With a meat pie.
The hatch has a lock. Seven pins. My mate says nobody's picked it.
Seven pins, quick ones with small green bands. One at a time.
It's open. The lantern's wired to a timer, and the timer is counting.
Five devices, and a new rule on the manual. Read them all in order every time.
Lantern five's dark. Two to go. The chip says: Chichen Itza, Mexico.
Diego is an archaeologist who sings. You'll hear him before you see him.
Twelve strips. Match the edges of the drawing and the writing.
The lantern's in the jaguar chamber, halfway up the serpent stairs, and there are guards on every step.
Six guards, two searchlights, and they walk fast. Wait, watch, then go.
I'm in the chamber. A ring lock on the jaguar's door. Five rings.
Five rings, each dragging the one outside it. Innermost first.
The jaguar's open. The lantern's panel is the biggest yet: five symbols from seven.
Five from seven, nine guesses. Think before every guess.
Lantern six's dark. And the chip's last line: "The seventh lantern stays with me. The mountain. O."
O. Otto. The Chairman. The Alps, Agent Rory. Klaus runs the cable car. This is the last one.
Kolya has taken the lantern core and my cousin's jeep. The jeep I can forgive. Vamonos!
Last one before the mountain, Rory. Steer clean and you will have him.
He went into the trees on foot and left the core behind. And a map of Switzerland with one valley circled.
Then that is where your Chairman keeps his cows. Ay. Good luck, amigo.
Six beams. The fastest yet. There is always a gap; find the rhythm.
Agent Rory. Welcome to my mountain. Do stop and talk. I insist.
You may ask me anything. I shall answer. Whether I answer truthfully is your problem.
He's on the intercom, and I've patched the polygraph into the line. His fibs are tiny. Look very hard.
So the seventh lantern IS in the mountain, the switch DOES turn off, and Eclipse is still here.
She is on the peak, waiting for a helicopter. Find the switch room first. There are a hundred rooms.
The switch room hums. Eight pings on a big grid. Make every one count.
Found it. The switch room. Seventy seconds on the clock and the Chairman's on the screen.
Seventy seconds, Agent Rory. Then seven cities go dark and the world pays me for the sunrise.
The abort code is five symbols this time. It's on the shredded map in your Dossier. Code, dial, wires. Go.
Switch... OFF. All seven lanterns dark.
Impossible. Nobody has ever... Kolya, do something!
Is not my job any more. I work at chip shop now.
Madame Eclipse slid off the peak on a tea tray. Straight into Dave's cab. He'd driven up the mountain. He said it was on the meter.
His star chart's still here. A bigger constellation this time, and a sky full of decoys. Join it in order.
The chart points down the terraces, to the lowest one, where nobody goes.
Loose stones instead of thin ice, same idea. Every solid stone tells you how many neighbours wobble. Go carefully.
Bottom terrace. There's a rope bridge here across the gorge, and something glinting on the far side.
The bridge is cut. Grapple gun. It's further this time and there's wind; aim into it.
Across. The fifth key was tied to the bridge post. And there's a set of gold scales in the temple with a note on them.
Twelve gold llamas and one is a fake, heavier than the rest. Three weighings on the temple scales. Make each one count.
The fake llama had a luggage tag inside. AMSTERDAM. And a tulip.
Amsterdam. Flat. You will miss the mountain.
Longer words now. Unscramble the lot's name.
Lot found: it's a crate of tulip pots, delivered to the flower market.
Five pots this time and the stallholder's hands are quick. The key's under one. Watch.
The sixth Prism Key. And under the next pot, a note: LOCK GATES.
Seven wires, properly tangled. Follow each one all the way; the gates only open when the panel is honest.
Gates open. A barge is coming through: the Curator's, loaded and listing.
It's about to tip and there's somebody's cat on board. Balance the cargo: weight times distance, both sides equal.
Level. The cat's fine. And the Curator's courier just pedalled off with the seventh key's shipping label.
Cargo bike, heading for the harbour. My bike is right there. Go!
Ring the bell and they move. Mostly.
Drag left and right to steer. Bollards, carts, bins: hit one and he pulls away.
Caught him at the harbour, and the label says ANTARCTICA. Dr Okafor's research station.
The bottom of the world, Agent Rory. Kolya's already on the plane. He's brought a thermos.
Whiteout. You'll see two steps ahead, if that. The walkways are a maze between the huts: tap the arrows, and trust the bits you've already lit.
Far hut. The seismographs are in here, all three, and they're all shaking.
Three stations, three distances, one vault. The rings are big out here and the tolerance is small. Lock it exactly.
The vault is two kilometres out on the shelf. There's a hut on top of it with a ledger inside.
I go too. I have thermos.
His ledger's a grid, and the combination for the vault door is the picture in it. Bigger grid. Take your time.
It's a snowflake. The door opened. Four keys on a velvet shelf, and the seventh already in the engine.
Naturally. Seven slots, Agent Rory, and you have carried me the two I was missing. Shall we?
The engine sings to the sky, and the sky comes down. Listen.
It's a signal, Rory. Match the aurora's own wave exactly, three dials, and the engine cancels itself. Lock it.
Locked. The engine's cancelled. The lights are... going back UP.
No. No, that is MINE.
He runs! Snowcat! Rory, the snowmobile!
The Curator's snowcat is fast but it's heavy. Ice chunks, fuel drums, flags and crevasses. Stay clean and you'll have him.
He hit a snowdrift. He's sitting in it. He says he'd like to complain to somebody.
The lights are back. All of them. Look up.
Evening, Agent Rory. Dave, M.I.S.T. wheelman. Lovely night for it. If you're a duck.
The Observatory's up the hill, past the phone box. The thieves changed the door code on their way out. Cheeky.
Rory, it's Vi. Walk with the left thumb, look with the right, and tap the green button when you reach something glowing.
